findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime-ordered audit logs
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to the ordered field value. The audit-log endpoint instantiates it with `order_by="-datetime"`, so for any non-empty result set `build_cursor` calls this method with a `datetime` and raises `TypeError`. Consequently, an administrator requesting `optimized_pagination=true` receives a 500 instead of audit-log results. This paginator needs the datetime cursor conversion used by `DateTimePaginator` (or should subclass it).

findings.title: Advanced negative offsets cause Django queryset slicing errors
findings.body: The advanced branch passes a negative `start_offset` directly to a Django `QuerySet` slice. Django explicitly rejects negative indexing/slicing on querysets with `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`, contrary to the comment's assertion that the ORM handles it. Cursor parsing accepts negative offsets, so an authorized caller using the advertised advanced negative-offset cursor capability can trigger a 500 response. Negative offsets must be translated to a supported query strategy or rejected as invalid pagination input.
